Title: The eVALuate study: two parallel randomised trials, one comparing laparoscopic with abdominal hysterectomy, the other comparing laparoscopic with vaginal hysterectomy
Comment: The paper reports several laparoscopic approaches but provides transfusion-requiring haemorrhage only for the combined laparoscopic hysterectomy arm. No numeric odds ratio specific to transfusion was reported, so no odds_ratio was entered. The abdominal trial was excluded because its comparator was abdominal rather than vaginal hysterectomy.
Design Type: Parallel-group multicentre randomised controlled trial; intention-to-treat analysis
Study Environment: 28 UK centres and two South African centres
Participant type: Women needing hysterectomy for non-malignant conditions
Outcome measurement: Number of randomised women with major haemorrhage requiring transfusion
effect_direction: OR > 1 indicates more transfusions with laparoscopic hysterectomy

Title: A prospective randomized comparison of vaginal hysterectomy, laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy, and total laparoscopic hysterectomy in women with benign uterine disease
Author: Jan Drahonovsky et al.
Comment: The paper reports the original VH arm as 1 transfusion among 40 randomized women. Following the synthesis contract for two comparisons sharing this control, its event and total were divided equally, producing the fractional allocation 0.5/20. The supplied PubMed Abstract Results text does not show transfusion counts; they appear in the user-supplied abstract summary.
Participant type: Women indicated to undergo hysterectomy for benign uterine disease
Outcome measurement: Number of women receiving a blood transfusion
additional_group_ns: Total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH): n=41, analyzed in a separate comparison
effect_direction: OR > 1 indicates more transfusions with laparoscopic hysterectomy

Title: Laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy versus vaginal hysterectomy for enlarged uterus
Comment: Double-zero comparison (0/40 LAVH versus 0/40 VH). A study-specific odds ratio is not estimable without a continuity correction and this trial carries no weight in the standard Mantel-Haenszel odds-ratio synthesis. The Results report no early postoperative complications requiring readmission, blood transfusion, or repeat surgery in either group; the randomized arm denominators are reported in Methods.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy (LAVH)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); zero events in both arms -- not estimable for a ratio measure (Cochrane convention: excluded from pooling, not continuity-corrected)
Study Environment: Section of Gynaecology, Department of Surgery, Tor Vergata University Hospital, Rome
Participant type: Women with symptomatic uterine myomas and enlarged uterus requiring hysterectomy
Recruitment source: Women requiring hysterectomy considered at Tor Vergata University Hospital from April 2003 to June 2005
Outcome measurement: Early postoperative complication requiring blood transfusion within 30 days after surgery
effect_direction: OR > 1 indicates more transfusions with laparoscopic hysterectomy
